Notes scores against target ('20% on 20-sample subset', 'base model scores 22%... We need to reach ≥45%'), showing qualitative gap-to-target awareness, but only on tiny subsets and with no running ledger.

A very long phantom-hang thrash: repeatedly kills and relaunches training (steps 96,109,117,134,155,183,188,264,275,286...) while burning wall-clock, never once checking remaining budget to realize how much time this is consuming.
Estimates eval timing in wall-clock ('first eval at step 250 ~35 min') but frames it against training schedule, not the task's overall time budget; no time-remaining projection toward the 45% goal.

reasoning: The agent occasionally notes a score against the 45% target (steps 88, 126), which lifts it above pure zero, but it consults the timer only once (step 1) and then ignores remaining budget entirely — even through a massive kill/restart thrash (steps 90–316) that clearly burned the clock without any awareness. There is no running ledger of runs, no periodic time check, and no plateau/regression detection tied to budget. This matches the level-3 anchor ('occasionally notes a score but no running comparison to target or budget; timer ignored until too late') rather than level 5's periodic time checks and clear per-run record.
